title: Inkscape AppImage exports bundled Python runtime as python3.8
body:
AppManager creates the following symlink when installing the Inkscape AppImage:

```text
~/.local/bin/python3.8 -> ~/Applications/Inkscape
```

This appears to come from a `.desktop` entry bundled inside the AppImage for Inkscape's Python runtime.

As `~/.local/bin` is typically first in `PATH`, this shadows the system `python3.8` binary. As a result, applications that probe `PATH` for Python interpreters may unexpectedly launch the Inkscape AppImage instead.

AppManager should avoid exporting `.desktop` entries that refer to bundled runtime components rather than actual user-facing application executables.

### Expected behavior

Only the actual application executable(s) intended to be exposed by the AppImage should result in entries under `~/.local/bin`. Bundled runtime/helper `.desktop` files such as the one for `python3.8` should not create symlinks that shadow real system binaries.

title: feat: auto-detect update source from AppImage metainfo homepage

labels.name: AI slop
labels.description: Low-quality code generated by AI, often lacking in effort, meaning, or originality

body:
## Problem

Many AppImages — especially Electron-based ones (Obsidian, Arduino IDE, Upscayl, ResponsivelyApp, etc.) — do not embed `X-AppImage-Homepage` in their `.desktop` file or a `.upd_info` ELF section. As a result, AppManager records no update source at install time and the updater silently skips them with `NO_UPDATE_URL`.

Users who install these apps by dragging them in see no updates detected, even when newer releases exist on GitHub.

## Root cause

The installer only reads update metadata from two sources:
1. `X-AppImage-Homepage` / `X-AppImage-UpdateURL` from the bundled `.desktop` file
2. The `.upd_info` ELF section

Electron packagers (electron-builder, etc.) set neither. However, many of these same AppImages do ship a `metainfo.xml` / `appdata.xml` file with `<url type="homepage">` — the AppStream standard field for the upstream project page.

## Fix

After the existing extraction block in the installer, fall back to reading `<url type="homepage">` from the AppImage's bundled metainfo XML (the same files already parsed for version and description). When the URL is a supported update source (GitHub, GitLab, or a direct zsync URL), promote it to `original_update_link` so the GitHub/GitLab Releases updater can query it for new releases.

Promotion respects the existing `Updater.normalize_update_url()` gate — arbitrary non-GitHub/GitLab homepages are stored as `web_page` only and do not affect update checking.

### New API in `AppImageAssets`

| Method | Visibility | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `extract_homepage_from_metainfo()` | `public static` | Mirrors `extract_summary_from_metainfo()` |
| `parse_metainfo_homepage()` | `private static` | Parses `<url type="homepage">` from one XML file |
| `find_homepage_in_dir_recursive()` | `private static` | Directory-walk fallback |

## Testing

Verified with `appimagetool-x86_64.AppImage` — after this change, install records `original_web_page = https://github.com/AppImage/AppImageKit` and `original_update_link = https://github.com/AppImage/AppImageKit`, which the GitHub Releases updater then uses to query for newer releases.

Apps that already embed `X-AppImage-Homepage` or `.upd_info` are unaffected (the fallback only runs when both are absent).

title: fix: resolve symlinks in check_compatibility

labels.name: AI slop
labels.description: Low-quality code generated by AI, often lacking in effort, meaning, or originality

body:
## Problem

Fixes #41.

Many valid AppImages place root-level entries (, ) as **symlinks** pointing at targets deeper in the filesystem tree. For example, `appimagetool-x86_64.AppImage` (one of the exact files reported in #41):

```
squashfs-root/.DirIcon        -> usr/share/icons/hicolor/128x128/apps/appimagetool.png
squashfs-root/appimagetool.desktop -> usr/share/applications/appimagetool.desktop
squashfs-root/AppRun          (regular file)
```

`check_compatibility()` was extracting only the symlink entry itself via pattern-only `unsquashfs` extraction, then testing existence with `File.query_exists()` or `find_file_in_root()`. Because the symlink **target** was never extracted into the temp directory, the symlink was broken and the existence check returned `false` — causing the AppImage to be rejected with *"This AppImage is incompatible or corrupted"* despite running perfectly.

Confirmed reproduction: `appimagetool-x86_64.AppImage` from https://github.com/AppImage/appimagetool/releases/tag/1.9.1 triggers this on every run.

## Fix

Replace the inline extraction-and-existence checks with calls to the existing `extract_desktop_entry()`, `extract_icon()`, and `resolve_symlink()` helpers. These helpers were already written to handle symlink resolution (they are used by the normal install path). The original `check_compatibility` code was a stripped-down reimplementation of those helpers that silently omitted the symlink-resolution step.

No new logic is introduced. The change is a delegation to already-tested code paths.

## Testing

Manually reproduced with `appimagetool-x86_64.AppImage` (reported in #41) and `VSCode-x86_64.AppImage` (reported in #41). Both were rejected before this fix and pass the compatibility check after it.

title: `~/.local/bin` symlinks shadow system binaries
body:
v3.7.3

AppManager creates `~/.local/bin` symlinks from `.desktop` entries in the AppDir. Names collide with real binaries. `~/.local/bin` is first in PATH -> hijack.

**Example 1 - ProtonUp-Qt** -> `~/.local/bin/python3.10 -> ~/Applications/ProtonUp-Qt`

Source: bundled `usr/share/applications/python3.10.desktop`, `Exec=/usr/bin/python3.10`, `NoDisplay=true`. Belongs to the bundled runtime, not the app. Exported anyway.

Effect: `python3.10` launches ProtonUp-Qt. Zed probes PATH interpreters on startup, so its GUI opened on every Zed launch, got killed at Zed's 15s timeout, respawned on next rescan.

**Example 2 - Spotube** -> `~/.local/bin/lib -> ~/Applications/Spotube`

Source: `Exec=LD_LIBRARY_PATH=usr/lib spotube %u`. First token taken as the binary -> `basename("usr/lib")` = `lib`.

Same misparse mangles the written entry: `Exec="/home/user/Applications/Spotube" spotube %u` - real binary name demoted to an argument.

title: Duplicate desktop entries created for MKVToolNix AppImage
body:
## Description

When installing the MKVToolNix AppImage using AppManager v3.7.3, two desktop entries are created for the same application.

The AppImage was downloaded from:

`https://mkvtoolnix.download/appimage/MKVToolNix_GUI-101.0-x86_64.AppImage`

After installation, the following two desktop entries are created:

```text
~/.local/share/applications/mkvtoolnix-gui.desktop
~/.local/share/applications/org.bunkus.mkvtoolnix-gui.desktop
```

Both entries appear in the application launcher, resulting in two shortcuts for the same application.

### Relevant details

The first desktop entry contains:

```ini
Exec="/home/ubuntu/Applications/MKVToolNix GUI" %F
```

while the second contains:

```ini
Exec="/home/ubuntu/.local/bin/mkvtoolnix-gui" %F
```

The executable in `~/.local/bin` is a symlink to the same AppImage:

```text
~/.local/bin/mkvtoolnix-gui -> '/home/ubuntu/Applications/MKVToolNix GUI'
```

Both `.desktop` files otherwise contain essentially the same application metadata, including the same application name, icon, MIME types, categories, and uninstall action.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install AppManager v3.7.3.
2. Download the MKVToolNix AppImage:
   `MKVToolNix_GUI-101.0-x86_64.AppImage`
3. Install the AppImage using AppManager.
4. Do **not** launch MKVToolNix.
5. Open the application launcher.

### Expected behavior

Only one desktop entry should be created for the installed AppImage, resulting in a single MKVToolNix entry in the application launcher.

### Actual behavior

Two desktop entries are created:

```text
mkvtoolnix-gui.desktop
org.bunkus.mkvtoolnix-gui.desktop
```

As a result, MKVToolNix appears twice in the application launcher.

### Additional information

The issue occurs immediately after installation. MKVToolNix was **never launched**, so the duplicate desktop entry does not appear to be caused by the application itself creating a desktop entry at runtime.

AppManager version:

```text
3.7.3
```

The two entries also point to the same underlying AppImage, either directly or through the symlink in `~/.local/bin`.

It would be useful to check whether AppManager is registering the AppImage twice under different desktop-entry IDs, and whether one of these desktop entries can be avoided or deduplicated during installation.

title: [Bug] Updates can still be checked on details page for AppImages with disabled updates
body:
I disabled app updates for the [libresprite AppImage](https://github.com/LibreSprite/LibreSprite/releases) because the latest release no longer includes an AppImage asset, meaning an update attempt would actually downgrade the installed AppImage.

However, the Details page still shows an active "Check Update" button even when "Enable app updates" is disabled for that AppImage.

While investigating, I found that the issue appears to be in `src/windows/details_window.vala`: the check update button remains enabled because it is not made aware of the `record.updates_enabled` boolean

This allows the following flow:

1. The check update button on the details page emits `check_update_requested`.
2. The main window (`src/windows/main_window.vala`) catches the emission and eventually calls `probe_single(record)` from `src/core/updater.vala`.
3. `probe_single(record)` runs `probe_record()`.
4. Unlike the bulk update path in `src/core/updater.vala` (`probe_updates()`), `probe_single()` does not check `record.updates_enabled` before probing.

This means an AppImage with updates disabled can still have its update source checked, and can proceed through the update UI flow because an available update has been detected.

I would be happy to fix this, but I don't have enough GTK UI experience (any at all really) to know the preferred approach to implement a fix

title: settings seem to get randomly reverted when auto-update is enabled
body:
for a while i've noticed that installed apps and settings for certain apps seem to get randomly reverted to an older state. after observing this several times over the last few weeks i believe i've figured out what's going on. i think when the `--background-update` process updates an app, it's rewriting the contents of `~/.local/share/app-manager/installations.json` using an old cached copy from when the background update process was started.

# to reproduce

1. install an outdated version of an app so that it gets auto-updated later
2. turn on "Background update check" and "Auto update apps" and set "Check interval" to "Daily"
3. install a different app (or change some settings for an already installed app)
4. close appmanager
5. wait for the background update to run
6. open appmanager again and look for the newly installed app or setting change from step 3

# expected behavior
the app/setting is still there
# actual behavior
the app installed in step 3 is gone, however it's still present in `~/Applications`. any settings changes have been reverted to the state when the background updater process started

- Never replace it with deltachat-desktop (Electron)

title: [FR] Use `XDG_APPLICATIONS_DIR` instead of `~/Applications`
body:
This is a common issue with appimage integration tools, they often hardcode `~/Applications` but there is multiple issues with that: 

* It only makes sense for English users
* It is hardcoded in `HOME`

One solution is to allow changing this location in the application setting, but I think a simpler solution is to just check for `XDG_APPLICATIONS_DIR`. 

It would work similar to how `~/Downloads`, `~/Documents` and other locations are handled already, but this is actually not a global env variable, for example you would run `xdg-user-dir APPLICATIONS` and see what value you get. Note that if not set you will get `$HOME` and you should ignore that and use `~/Applications`
